author: alexsanderhamir
body:
This PR adds a setup script (`setup.sh`) that significantly reduces friction for developers who want to build and try the project locally.

## What's included

- Automated dependency installation (Python + Node.js)
- Virtual environment setup and activation
- API key configuration
- Simple terminal option to start both servers immediately
- Updated README with clear setup instructions

## Additional Changes

The PR now also addresses a bug where analysis history would save even when there were errors. This includes:

- Server-side error handling that returns structured error responses
- Client-side logic that only saves successful analyses to history
- Visual distinction between successful and failed analyses in the history
- Better user feedback through toast notifications
- Type-safe error handling across the application

## Add-ons

1. Fixed some lack of error handling that could cause issues.

### [`v1.17.2`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/releases/tag/v1.17.2): MongoDB Go Driver 1.17.2

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/compare/v1.17.1...v1.17.2)

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 1.17.2 of the official MongoDB Go driver.

#### Release Notes

This release addresses several issues and tasks to improve the functionality of the Go Driver. It includes a fix for a bug in the `DefaultValueDecoders.ValueUnmarshalerDecodeValue` to avoid  inappropriately instantiating a pointer field decoded from null data if the user defined an `UnmarshalBSONValue`. Additionally, the release resolves a goroutine and memory leak issue found in the Zstandard (zstd) network compression decoding process.

Furthermore, the release includes a task to restore the `ReadCompressedCompressedMessage()` function to the wiremessage API. This function was previously removed under task GODRIVER-3303 with the aim of preventing out-of-bounds runtime errors, as it was identified as complicit in such issues and was not needed by the driver itself. author: copilot
body:
Plugin managers (lazy.nvim, packer, etc.) were unable to update the MyST extension due to local git changes in injection query files:

```
Your local changes in .local/share/nvim/lazy/myst-markdown-tree-sitter-v3.nvim
   * queries/markdown/injections.scm
   * queries/myst/injections.scm
 Please remove them to update.
```

## Root Cause

The plugin was dynamically generating and writing injection query files at runtime in `setup_injection_queries()` to support configurable default languages. This created local modifications that git detected as uncommitted changes, preventing plugin updates.

## Solution

- Removed all file writing from `setup_injection_queries()` function
- Plugin now relies entirely on static query files committed to the repository
- Static files provide identical functionality with Python as the default language for `{code-cell}` blocks

## Trade-offs

**Fixed:**
- Plugin updates now work without conflicts
- No more local git changes during operation

**Preserved:**
- All 14 supported language injections for MyST code-cells (python, javascript, bash, r, julia, c, cpp, rust, go, typescript, etc.)
- LaTeX math highlighting support via `markdown_inline` parser
- All core MyST highlighting functionality

**Limited:**
- `default_code_cell_language` configuration option is no longer functional
- Defaults to Python for `{code-cell}` blocks without explicit language

The plugin prioritizes usability (updates work) over configuration flexibility. Future versions may restore configurable defaults using methods that don't cause git conflicts.

Fixes #21.

author: adamchalmers
body:
Adds a new constraint for the angle between two lines. It's (line0, line1, angle).

This is a very general-purpose constraint. LinesParallel and LinesPerpendicular are two special cases of this constraint when angle is 0 and 90 respectively. So rather than add new constraints for those special cases, I just made convenience constructors for those cases. This keeps the simple system (fewer constraints means fewer math equations to review and maintain), but still convenient for users (because common uses have convenient named constructors).

Added a test too.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

In live ETW/EventPipe sessions using TraceLog, `RelatedActivityID` and `ContainerID` appear empty even when emitted by providers. This occurs because `ProcessExtendedData` mutates `EVENT_RECORD.ExtendedData` and `ExtendedDataCount` fields during ingestion, overwriting the original data with persistence indexes. Later, when readers like `TraceEventSource.GetRelatedActivityID()` attempt to access the data from `ExtendedData`, they find indexes instead of the actual GUID values.

## Root Cause

The `ProcessExtendedData` method was designed for file conversion workflows where:
1. RelatedActivityID/ContainerID are extracted from `ExtendedData` 
2. Stored in persistent arrays (`relatedActivityIDs`, `containerIDs`)
3. `ExtendedData` pointer is overwritten with an array index
4. `ExtendedDataCount` is overwritten with an array index

This works for file-based traces because the `GetRelatedActivityID()` method reads from the persistent arrays using these indexes. However, in live sessions, this mutation destroys the original data that EventPipe readers expect to access directly.

## Solution

Added a `isLiveSession` parameter to `ProcessExtendedData` that:

- **When `false` (file conversion)**: Preserves existing behavior - persists RelatedActivityID/ContainerID and modifies ExtendedData pointers
- **When `true` (live sessions)**: Skips persistence and leaves ExtendedData intact for direct reader access

## Changes

1. **ProcessExtendedData signature**: Added `bool isLiveSession = false` parameter with comprehensive documentation
2. **Live session preservation**: Skip RelatedActivityID/ContainerID extraction and ExtendedData mutation when `isLiveSession = true`
3. **Live ingestion paths**: Updated `onAllEventsRealTime` and `OnAllEventPipeEventsRealTime` to pass `isLiveSession: true`
4. **File conversion unchanged**: All existing file conversion calls use the default `false` value

## Verification

The fix ensures that:
- **Live sessions**: EventPipe and ETW readers can access RelatedActivityID/ContainerID from original ExtendedData
- **File conversion**: Continues to work exactly as before with no behavioral changes
- **Backwards compatibility**: Maintained through default parameter values

This resolves the issue where live EventPipe + TraceLog sessions showed empty RelatedActivityID values despite providers emitting them correctly.

body: Original ticket PR #739 only delivered modal wiring and documented a draft schema; this PR completes the UI to match the finalized backend. It delivers end-to-end support for importing multiple tools via JSON file upload or paste, enforcing validation rules, and handling partial success cases. # Key Changes ## Frontend (admin.html / JS) Added Bulk Import modal with: - Drag-and-drop JSON file upload support. - JSON paste input with real-time debounce validation. ## Backend - Endpoint: `POST /admin/tools/import` - Authentication: Admin only, JWT-based. - Rate limiting: 10 requests/minute. - Transaction-safe batch persistence with rollback support. ``` { "success": true, "created_count": 2, "failed_count": 0, "created": [{"index":0,"name":"tool_1"},{"index":1,"name":"tool_2"}], "errors": [] } ``` ## Configuration Environment variables required: ``` export MCPGATEWAY_UI_ENABLED=true export MCPGATEWAY_ADMIN_API_ENABLED=true export BASIC_AUTH_USER=admin export BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD=admin export JWT_SECRET_KEY=my-test-key export MCPGATEWAY_BULK_IMPORT_ENABLED="true" ``` ## Validation Rules - Tool name must start with a letter and contain only alphanumeric or underscores. - Required fields: name, url, description. - Optional fields: integration type, request type, tags, headers, auth. - Maximum: 200 tools per batch. - File format supported: JSON array only. ## Testing Scenarios - Successful batch import of 10 tools. Ex: ``` [ { "name": "Tool_A", "url": "https://api.example.com/alpha", "description": "Alpha test tool for bulk import", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "GET", "tags": ["alpha", "test", "api"] }, { "name": "Tool_B", "url": "https://api.example.com/beta", "description": "Beta test tool for bulk import", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "POST", "tags": ["beta", "import"] }, { "name": "Tool_C", "url": "https://service.example.com/gamma", "description": "Gamma service integration", "integration_type": "MCP", "request_type": "GET", "headers": { "Accept": "application/json" } }, { "name": "Tool_D", "url": "http://localhost:8080/delta", "description": "Local delta tool for testing", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "POST" }, { "name": "Tool_E", "url": "https://tools.example.com/epsilon", "description": "Epsilon tool description", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "GET", "tags": ["epsilon", "utility"] }, { "name": "Tool_F", "url": "https://api.example.com/zeta", "description": "Zeta bulk import test", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "POST", "auth": { "type": "basic", "username": "user", "password": "pass" } }, { "name": "Tool_G", "url": "https://service.example.com/eta", "description": "Eta example service", "integration_type": "MCP", "request_type": "GET" }, { "name": "Tool_H", "url": "https://tools.example.com/theta", "description": "Theta integration tool", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "POST", "tags": ["theta", "integration", "api"] }, { "name": "Tool_I", "url": "https://api.example.com/iota", "description": "Iota test API tool", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "GET" }, { "name": "Tool_J", "url": "https://service.example.com/kappa", "description": "Kappa service test tool", "integration_type": "REST", "request_type": "POST", "tags": ["kappa", "test"] } ] ``` - Invalid JSON syntax error handling. - Duplicate name rejection. - Partial success when some tools are invalid. - Import rate limit enforcement.

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a Node.js script `scripts/patch-index-html.mjs` that transforms the Expo web entry script to use ES module syntax for better compatibility.

## What it does

The script reads `dist/index.html` and converts Expo entry script tags from:
```html
<script src="/_expo/static/js/web/entry-...js" defer></script>
```

To:
```html
<script type="module" src="/_expo/static/js/web/entry-...js"></script>
```

## Why this is needed

Modern web applications often require ES module syntax for proper loading and execution. This transformation:
- Removes the `defer` attribute which is not needed with `type="module"`
- Adds `type="module"` to enable ES module loading
- Ensures compatibility with build tools and deployment environments that expect ES modules

## Implementation details

The script uses two regex patterns to handle different scenarios:
1. Script tags with `defer` attribute (most common case)
2. Script tags without `defer` (fallback case)

After running, the script outputs a confirmation message: `✅ Patched dist/index.html to use type="module" for Expo entry.`

## Usage

Run the script after building the web version:
```bash
npm run build-web
node scripts/patch-index-html.mjs
```

Previously, users could only view one team's roster at a time after selecting from a dropdown, making it difficult to compare keeper options and costs across multiple teams without repeatedly switching views.

This commit introduces a "View All Teams" button that displays all team rosters in a single, high-density grid layout. The view shows normalized team names in proper case and simplified player information (names and keeper costs only), enabling quick comparison of keeper options across the entire league. The feature includes responsive design and navigation between the team selection and all-teams views.

This pull request introduces the CKBFS Protocol V3, which brings significant changes to the file storage protocol and updates the smart contract implementations for compatibility. The main improvements focus on moving backlinks from cell data to witnesses, updating witness structure and validation logic, and refactoring contract code to support the new protocol version. Key changes are grouped below:

**CKBFS Protocol V3 Specification and Data Model:**

* Added comprehensive documentation for CKBFS Protocol V3 in `RFC.v3.md`, detailing new cell structure, witness format, and operational rules, including the migration of backlinks to witnesses and updated checksum handling.

**Smart Contract Logic Updates for V3:**

* Implemented support for V3 witness validation in the `ckb-adler32` contract, including new logic for loading and chaining witness parts, extracting metadata, and validating checksums according to the V3 specification. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ee936c56a18615416311694d4a86c641a4b30f878219bc033550df3f8e79a54fR22-R124) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ee936c56a18615416311694d4a86c641a4b30f878219bc033550df3f8e79a54fR212-R277) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b7b41bfccb8d3f86134fa21dc9277704d1d525586e129b141bbfe64fa96134dcR61-R63)
* Refactored witness validation entry points in the `ckbfs` contract to use the new V3 witness chain and checksum validation logic, replacing the previous multi-index approach. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-89e5e2f0709cb4ef3d0e5add620d61d3061bde81d7b4001cec3a1559d1b03f76L72-R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-89e5e2f0709cb4ef3d0e5add620d61d3061bde81d7b4001cec3a1559d1b03f76L84-R87) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-89e5e2f0709cb4ef3d0e5add620d61d3061bde81d7b4001cec3a1559d1b03f76L102-R98) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-89e5e2f0709cb4ef3d0e5add620d61d3061bde81d7b4001cec3a1559d1b03f76L115-R116)

**Cell Creation and Validation Refactor:**

* Updated cell creation and validation logic to remove backlinks handling, add previous position validation for witnesses, and ensure correct initialization and checksum verification for V3 cells.

**Dependency and Build Configuration Updates:**

* Bumped `ckbfs-types` dependency to version `0.3.0` in `contracts/ckbfs/Cargo.toml` to ensure compatibility with new data structures.
* Updated `Makefile` to use the correct Rust debug assertions flag for improved build reliability.

CLOSES: #3

## Summary

This PR implements the initial project setup for the D&D Combat Tracker, initializing a Next.js 15 application with TypeScript and all required core dependencies.

## Changes Made

### Core Setup
- ✅ Created Next.js 15 app with TypeScript and strict mode enabled
- ✅ Configured pnpm as package manager with proper packageManager field
- ✅ Set up ESLint and Prettier configurations with Next.js standards
- ✅ Created initial folder structure: `src/{app,components,lib,hooks,models,types,styles}`

### Development Configuration
- ✅ Configured path aliases in tsconfig.json (`@/*`, `@/../*`, `@/components/*`, etc.)
- ✅ Set up Jest testing framework with proper module mapping for path aliases
- ✅ Added TailwindCSS for styling with PostCSS configuration
- ✅ Added comprehensive .gitignore for Next.js project structure

### Testing & Quality
- ✅ Implemented TDD approach with comprehensive setup validation tests
- ✅ All tests passing (6/6 tests pass)
- ✅ Build successful with no errors
- ✅ ESLint clean with no warnings or errors
- ✅ Proper ES6 imports using path aliases instead of relative paths

### File Structure Created
```
src/
├── app/
│   ├── globals.css
│   ├── layout.tsx
│   └── page.tsx
├── components/
│   └── Welcome.tsx
├── lib/
│   └── utils.ts
├── hooks/
│   └── useWelcome.ts
├── models/
│   └── Character.ts
├── types/
│   └── welcome.ts
└── __tests__/
    └── setup.test.ts
```

## Testing

- ✅ All setup validation tests pass
- ✅ Next.js dev server starts successfully
- ✅ Build process completes without errors
- ✅ Path aliases work correctly in imports
- ✅ TypeScript strict mode enabled and working

## Acceptance Criteria Met

- [x] Next.js app runs locally with no errors on `pnpm dev`
- [x] TypeScript is enabled and strict mode is on; no `any` types used without justification
- [x] pnpm is used for all package management; `pnpm install` completes with no errors
- [x] ESLint and Prettier are configured and `pnpm run lint` passes on all code
- [x] Git repository is initialized, first commit is pushed, and remote is set up
- [x] Folder structure matches the specification exactly
- [x] Path aliases work as expected in all imports (demonstrated by working imports)
- [x] All new setup steps are documented through configuration files
- [x] Failing tests written before implementation (TDD approach)
- [x] All initial tests pass after implementation

## Summary
- Introduces a new SSE server implemented as a Cloudflare Durable Object for managing Server-Sent Events connections
- Adds webhook handler with retry and fallback support for notification delivery
- Implements rate limiting and health check API endpoints
- Adds a Next.js frontend app with Tailwind CSS and ESLint configuration
- Integrates PocketBase for notification history storage

## Changes

### SSE Server
- Created `SSEConnectionManager` Durable Object to handle SSE connections, pings, notifications, and cleanup
- Added API routes for SSE connection management (`/connect`, `/notify`, `/disconnect`, `/status`)
- Implemented notification sending to individual connections or all connections of a user
- Added rate limiting using KV store
- Added health check endpoint `/api/health`

### Webhook Handler
- Added `WebhookHandler` class to process webhook notifications with support for primary and fallback URLs
- Logs notification delivery status to PocketBase
- Implements queue consumer for webhook processing with retries

### Frontend (Next.js)
- Added new Next.js app under `apps/web` with initial setup, components, hooks, and utilities
- Configured Tailwind CSS and ESLint for frontend development
- Added PocketBase client integration and SSE client hook

### Configuration and Tooling
- Added `wrangler.toml` for SSE server deployment with environment variables, Durable Object, KV, and queue bindings
- Added TypeScript configurations for SSE server and shared packages
- Added package.json and lock files for dependencies management

- [x] Test rate limiting enforcement on notification API
- [x] Test Next.js frontend rendering and SSE client hook

**Backend: Django/MongoDB Integration and API Setup**

将平台从一个通用的笔记服务转换为一个由 arXiv 驱动的个性化 RAG 系统，具备完整的论文摄取、查询、电子邮件订阅以及用户可配置的 RAG 设置功能。

新功能：
- 实现每日 arXiv 论文摄取管道，使用 Celery Beat 和 Prefect，并采用 PostgreSQL、MinIO 和 Qdrant 进行存储
- 添加基于 GraphRAG 的订阅服务，用于向用户发送主题性每日电子邮件摘要
- 引入持久化用户系统设置（语言、翻译、提示词、RAG 参数），存储在 Redis 和 PostgreSQL 中，并提供新的 API 端点和前端设置 UI
- 扩展领域模型，使其包含论文 (Papers) 以及用户笔记 (Notes)，并相应地更新所有 CRUD 操作和仪表板统计数据
- 增强查询流程，增加可选的翻译、查询重写和多步骤 Agentic RAG 推理功能

改进：
- 将 PRD 文档重写为一个全面的以 arXiv 为中心的需求规范，包含架构图和 FRD/NFR 部分
- 重构摄取逻辑，移除遗留的后台线程，转而使用 Celery 工作流
- 添加统一的日志记录功能，同时输出到文件和控制台，并集中管理跨服务的配置

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>onsi/ginkgo (github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2)</summary>

### [`v2.25.0`](https://redirect.github.com/onsi/ginkgo/releases/tag/v2.25.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/onsi/ginkgo/compare/v2.24.0...v2.25.0)

#### 2.25.0

##### `AroundNode`

This release introduces a new decorator to support more complex spec setup usecases.

`AroundNode` registers a function that runs before each individual node.  This is considered a more advanced decorator.

Please read the [docs](https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/#advanced-around-node) for more information and some examples.

Allowed signatures:

- `AroundNode(func())` - `func` will be called before the node is run.
- `AroundNode(func(ctx context.Context) context.Context)` - `func` can wrap the passed in context and return a new one which will be passed on to the node.
- `AroundNode(func(ctx context.Context, body func(ctx context.Context)))` - `ctx` is the context for the node and `body` is a function that must be called to run the node.  This gives you complete control over what runs before and after the node.

Multiple `AroundNode` decorators can be applied to a single node and they will run in the order they are applied.

Unlike setup nodes like `BeforeEach` and `DeferCleanup`, `AroundNode` is guaranteed to run in the same goroutine as the decorated node.  This is necessary when working with lower-level libraries that must run on a single thread (you can call `runtime.LockOSThread()` in the `AroundNode` to ensure that the node runs on a single thread).

Since `AroundNode` allows you to modify the context you can also use `AroundNode` to implement shared setup that attaches values to the context.

If applied to a container, `AroundNode` will run before every node in the container.  Including setup nodes like `BeforeEach` and `DeferCleanup`.

`AroundNode` can also be applied to `RunSpecs` to run before every node in the suite.  This opens up new mechanisms for instrumenting individual nodes across an entire suite.

</details>

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses the issue of having "a lot of unnecessary files and stuff for simple local dev" by significantly streamlining the project structure and removing complex features that were overkill for local development.

## Problem
The project had accumulated many complex features and files that made local development slower and more complicated:
- Build failures due to broken scripts with Prisma type issues
- 183MB of build artifacts being committed to git
- Complex testing infrastructure (Playwright, Jest) for simple development
- Heavy dependencies (Elasticsearch, Sharp, Winston) adding overhead
- Production-specific scripts and documentation cluttering the workspace
- Inconsistent package management (both npm and yarn lock files)

## Solution
Performed a comprehensive cleanup focused on **simple local development experience**:

### Removed Complex Features
- **Performance optimization libraries** (`src/lib/performance/`) - image optimization, preloading, web vitals
- **Advanced search functionality** (`src/lib/search/`) - Elasticsearch integration
- **SEO/slug features** (`src/lib/slug*`, `src/lib/seo.ts`) - causing build failures due to Prisma type issues
- **Testing infrastructure** - Playwright E2E tests, Jest unit tests, manual test scripts
- **Production deployment scripts** - checklist scripts, sample data generators

### Cleaned Up Project Structure
- **Removed documentation files** - status updates and implementation docs (12KB)
- **Removed build artifacts** - `.next/` cache (183MB), TypeScript build info
- **Standardized package management** - removed `yarn.lock`, kept `package-lock.json`
- **Updated .gitignore** - prevent build artifacts from being committed again

### Simplified Dependencies
Removed heavy dependencies that were overkill for local dev:
```diff
- "@elastic/elasticsearch": "^9.1.1"
- "elasticsearch": "^16.7.3"
- "sharp": "^0.34.3"
- "socket.io": "^4.8.1"
- "winston": "^3.17.0"
- "web-vitals": "^5.1.0"
- "@playwright/test": "^1.54.2"
- "jest": "^29.7.0"
```

## Results
- **Startup time**: Now consistently ~1.4 seconds (vs much longer before)
- **Dependencies**: Reduced from 842 to 467 packages
- **File count**: Reduced from 280+ to 131 files  
- **Code removed**: ~13,000+ lines of complex code
- **Build size**: No more 183MB cache artifacts

## What Still Works
All core functionality remains intact:
- ✅ Game listing and viewing pages
- ✅ API endpoints for games  
- ✅ Authentication system
- ✅ Database integration with Prisma
- ✅ Tailwind CSS styling
- ✅ TypeScript compilation
- ✅ Next.js development server

The removed features can be re-added later when the project scales and actually needs them. This cleanup prioritizes a fast, clean development experience for simple local work.

See `CLEANUP_SUMMARY.md` for detailed information about what was removed and why.

body:
## Problem
The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation uses a large graph size (20 nodes) with no rate limiting or timeouts, causing excessive CPU consumption.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms sleep between iterations for rate limiting
- Implemented 5-second timeout per path calculation
- Reduced max path depth from 10 to 5 for brute force algorithm
- Added early termination if calculation exceeds timeout

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed functionality maintains correct path finding capabilities
- Tested with continuous operation without pod restarts

## Impact
This change will prevent pod restarts due to CPU spikes while maintaining core functionality. CPU usage should stay below critical thresholds.

body: # MERICATrader Core Scaffolding & Initial API ## Overview This PR establishes the foundational architecture for the MERICATrader application, implementing the specified tech stack and core data model. It sets up the initial API endpoints for inventory and listings, with a strong emphasis on data integrity and server-side security, laying the groundwork for the local-first marketplace MVP. ## Changes Made ### 1. Core Application Setup - ✅ Initialized Next.js 14 App Router project with Tailwind CSS and TypeScript. - ✅ Configured essential project files (`.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `next.config.mjs`, `globals.css`, `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`). ### 2. Database & ORM Integration - ✅ Set up Drizzle ORM with PostgreSQL connection. - ✅ Defined comprehensive Drizzle schemas for all core entities: `users`, `user_profiles`, `inventory_lots`, `inventory_movements`, `listings`, `carts`, `cart_items`, `orders`, `order_items`, and `watchlists`. - ✅ Implemented lazy database connection to prevent build-time errors. ### 3. Authentication & Authorization - ✅ Integrated NextAuth with a Credentials provider for user authentication. - ✅ Implemented `requireUser` helper for server-side route protection, ensuring authenticated access to mutations. ### 4. Data Validation - ✅ Created Zod schemas (`createInventoryLotSchema`, `createListingSchema`) for robust server-side and client-side input validation. ### 5. Inventory & Listing API Endpoints - ✅ Developed `POST` and `GET` endpoints for `/api/inventory/lots`, including initial inventory movement creation upon lot creation to establish quantity truth. - ✅ Implemented `POST`, `GET`, and `PUT` (for publishing) endpoints for `/api/listings`, with `quantity_available` derived from the movements ledger upon publishing. - ✅ Added `GET /api/listings/[id]` for individual listing retrieval. - ✅ Created `GET /api/me` to retrieve current user and profile data. ## Testing The project successfully compiles (`next build`) after all changes, indicating a stable foundational setup. ## Implementation Notes - This PR focuses on establishing the core backend logic and data structures as per the prompt's "Operating Rules" and "Quantity Truth" sections. - Server-side guards (`requireUser`) are in place for critical mutations. - The `inventory_movements` ledger is used to track quantity changes, ensuring data consistency. - Further API endpoints (cart, checkout, search) and UI pages will be built upon this foundation. ## Related Issues - Resolves #XX: Initial scaffolding and core API implementation for MERICATrader. ## Screenshots [Optional: Add screenshots of successful deployment logs] ---

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses missing detailed EPA descriptions in the interactive ecoregion map. The map includes a "Learn More" button that displays official EPA detailed descriptions for each Level 4 ecoregion, but several ecoregions were missing these detailed descriptions.

## Issue
Users clicking on ecoregions `50t` (North Shore Highlands) and `52c` (Rochester/Paleozoic Plateau Upland) would not see the "Learn More" button because their detailed descriptions were missing from the `detailedDescriptions` object, even though they had brief summaries in `ecoregionDescriptions`.

## Changes Made
Added detailed EPA descriptions for 9 missing ecoregions to the `detailedDescriptions` object:

- **50t** (North Shore Highlands): Spectacular Lake Superior shoreline landscape
- **51a** (St. Croix Stagnation Moraines): Twin Cities metropolitan area 
- **51h** (Anoka Sand Plain): Sandy outwash plains and terraces
- **51i** (Big Woods): Distinctive hardwood forest ecoregion
- **51j** (Alexandria Moraines): Western Minnesota moraines and lakes
- **51k** (McGrath Till Plain): Transition from forest to agriculture
- **51l** (Wadena/Todd Drumlins): Rolling terrain between moraines  
- **52b** (Blufflands and Coulees): Deeply dissected terrain
- **52c** (Rochester/Paleozoic Plateau Upland): Gently rolling plateau

All descriptions were sourced from the official EPA documentation provided in issue #5.

## Verification
- ✅ All 32 ecoregions now have both brief and detailed descriptions
- ✅ JavaScript syntax validation passes
- ✅ Comprehensive audit confirms no missing entries

![Test Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec10441d-9065-4d1a-9390-817cb9127049)

The "Learn More" functionality now works for all ecoregions, providing users with comprehensive EPA detailed descriptions alongside the existing brief summaries.

Fixes #7.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses the missing README documentation by creating a comprehensive guide for the earthquake MVP project and fixes several critical issues in the data visualization pipeline.

## Changes Made

### 📚 Added Comprehensive README.md
Created a detailed 206-line README that includes:
- Project overview and feature descriptions
- Complete installation and setup instructions
- Usage documentation for all components (Make commands, Streamlit dashboard, Docker)
- Detailed project structure explanation
- Data sources and pipeline documentation
- Development guidelines and troubleshooting section

### 🐛 Fixed Critical Visualization Bugs
1. **Negative magnitude handling**: Fixed crash when plotting earthquakes with negative magnitudes by clipping size values to a minimum of 0.1
2. **Column name mismatch**: Corrected `depth_km` references to `depth` to match actual data structure
3. **Test execution**: Fixed Makefile test command to use proper `PYTHONPATH` for module imports

### 🔧 Infrastructure Improvements
- Updated `.gitignore` to exclude temporary data files
- Enhanced error handling in visualization scripts
- Added directory creation for map output

## Technical Details

The visualization scripts were failing due to Plotly's size parameter not accepting negative values, which occurred with some earthquake magnitudes. The fix ensures all earthquakes are displayable while preserving the relative magnitude information through color coding.

Before:
```python
size="magnitude",  # Fails with negative values
hover_data=["time_iso", "depth_km"],  # Wrong column name
```

After:
```python
df['size_magnitude'] = df['magnitude'].clip(lower=0.1)
size="size_magnitude",  # Always positive
hover_data=["time_iso", "depth"],  # Correct column name
```

## Validation
- All Make pipeline commands (`fetch`, `process`, `visualize`, `test`) now work correctly
- Tests pass with proper module path resolution
- Generated interactive maps display properly with 10,000+ earthquake data points
- Streamlit dashboard functionality verified

The project now has complete documentation and a fully functional data pipeline ready for users to analyze real-time earthquake data from USGS.

# Pull Request Checklist

### Note to first-time contributors: Please open a discussion post in [Discussions](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/discussions) and describe your changes before submitting a pull request.

**Before submitting, make sure you've checked the following:**

- [ ] **Target branch:** Please verify that the pull request targets the `dev` branch.
- [ ] **Description:** Provide a concise description of the changes made in this pull request.
- [ ] **Changelog:** Ensure a changelog entry following the format of [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/) is added at the bottom of the PR description.
- [ ] **Documentation:** Have you updated relevant documentation [Open WebUI Docs](https://github.com/open-webui/docs), or other documentation sources?
- [ ] **Dependencies:** Are there any new dependencies? Have you updated the dependency versions in the documentation?
- [ ] **Testing:** Have you written and run sufficient tests to validate the changes?
- [ ] **Code review:** Have you performed a self-review of your code, addressing any coding standard issues and ensuring adherence to the project's coding standards?
- [ ] **Prefix:** To clearly categorize this pull request, prefix the pull request title using one of the following:
  - **BREAKING CHANGE**: Significant changes that may affect compatibility
  - **build**: Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
  - **ci**: Changes to our continuous integration processes or workflows
  - **chore**: Refactor, cleanup, or other non-functional code changes
  - **docs**: Documentation update or addition
  - **feat**: Introduces a new feature or enhancement to the codebase
  - **fix**: Bug fix or error correction
  - **i18n**: Internationalization or localization changes
  - **perf**: Performance improvement
  - **refactor**: Code restructuring for better maintainability, readability, or scalability
  - **style**: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code (white space, formatting, missing semi-colons, etc.)
  - **test**: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
  - **WIP**: Work in progress, a temporary label for incomplete or ongoing work

author: sunrabbit123
body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the build process and code formatting for the VSCode extension and the compiler package. The most notable changes are the switch from Prettier to Biome for code formatting and import organization, the addition of Biome dependencies, and enhancements to the post-build script to support multiple WASM files.

**Build and formatting improvements:**

* Switched code formatting and import sorting in `FilePrinter.beautify` from Prettier and related plugins to the Biome formatter, using the Biome JS API for more robust and configurable formatting and import organization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-43b5467f1f00bc6955ef675360b7d8a7dc2691e5b8cd2105215931a1960ec698L1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43b5467f1f00bc6955ef675360b7d8a7dc2691e5b8cd2105215931a1960ec698L44-R70)
* Added `@biomejs/js-api` and `@biomejs/wasm-bundler` dependencies to `packages/compiler/package.json` and removed Prettier and related plugins, reflecting the formatter migration.

**Build script enhancements:**

* Refactored `apps/vscode-extension/worker/build/postbuild.js` to use ES module imports, added support for copying both Prisma and Biome WASM files, and implemented a generic `copyWasmFile` function for extensibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e5cb61c593c43148174ef4e2a6f18e22e1ebb8a5fd9790142bc8fab54618a339L1-R44) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e5cb61c593c43148174ef4e2a6f18e22e1ebb8a5fd9790142bc8fab54618a339L31-R66)
* Updated the logic for finding WASM files in `.pnpm` directories to support both Prisma and Biome WASM packages.
* Modified the `vscode:pack` script in `apps/vscode-extension/package.json` to use `vsce pack --no-dependencies` for more controlled packaging.

body: ## JIRA or Github ticker * [160](https://github.com/ita-social-projects/VictoryCenter-Back/issues/160) ## Description Created generic SearchBar component that can work with any data with custom rendering. Custom rendering requires component with forwardRef hook. Refactored other part of program page code base for better maintainability. Developed 3 generic hooks for easy async data fetch. Developed tooltip with 2 display mods (absolute positioning by nearest relative parent or render in portal basing on positioner) ## How it looks ## Summary of change - Generic search bar with default rendering - Generic hooks for data fetch with cancellation handling - Group inputs in forms into groups component - Tooltip components with 2 displaye mods - Refactor styling in input components of admin page - Refactor Programs page - Reusable functionality hooks, like useObserveElementSize, useScrollHandler or useDebouncedValueCallback. ## How to recreate changes 1) Start frontend 2) Go to https://localhost:3000/admin-panel/programs 3) Use search bar ## CHECK LIST - [ ] New tests was added or existing was modified - [ ] Changes has severe impact on users - [ ] Changes has medium impact on users - [ ] Changes has light impact on users - [ ] Test covetage was updated - [ ] PR meets all conventions ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Rich, typed search with debounced suggestions, keyboard navigation, per-item tooltips, and selectable suggestions. * New tooltip component (portal support) and new grouped input controls (single/multi-select, character-limited inputs/areas, photo input, input error). * Centralized modal orchestration for Programs and suggestion-driven toolbar search. * **Enhancements** * Improved accessibility (ARIA, keyboard), outside-click behavior, paginated/debounced fetching, consistent styling and clearer image fallbacks. * **Tests** * Large expansion of unit and hook tests across components and pages.

## Description

Added functionality to detect and upgrade published components within the pipeline. This PR introduces a new UI for displaying published component details, checking for updates, and upgrading tasks to newer component versions.

Key changes:
- Added a published component badge to task nodes
- Created a component details panel showing published status and version information
- Implemented a force update mechanism to upgrade tasks using outdated components
- Added a dialog context to manage component detail dialogs
- Created a popover UI for upgrading nodes with confirmation workflow

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Improvement

## Checklist

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dd23b11-6bdb-4090-ba3f-47f930de5d8b



1. Enable the "remote-component-library-search" beta flag
2. Create a task using a published component
3. Verify the published component badge appears on the task
4. Open component details to see published status

This feature is behind the "remote-component-library-search" beta flag and builds on the existing component library infrastructure.

author: maxy-shpfy
body:
## Description

This PR enhances component upgrade functionality by improving how outdated components are managed and displayed in the UI. It adds visual indicators for outdated components and implements a more robust upgrade mechanism.

## Type of Change

- [x] Improvement
- [x] New feature

## Checklist

- [x] I have tested this does not break current pipelines / runs functionality
- [x] I have tested the changes on staging

## Key Changes

1. Modified `useForceUpdateTasks` to use a Map for component replacement, allowing multiple components to be updated at once
2. Added visual indicators for outdated components in the sidebar:
    - Alert badge on folder items
    - Orange warning icon for outdated components
3. Created a new `UpgradeAvailableAlertBox` component that shows when outdated components are detected
4. Implemented a dismissal system for upgrade alerts (24-hour cooldown)
5. Added a "Review" button to batch upgrade all outdated components
6. Updated the `NodesOverlayProvider` to handle multiple component upgrades
7. Enhanced typed storage utility to support custom encoders/decoders

## Test Instructions

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4331af14-ea85-4466-bc04-7b116eb78e0d

1. Add outdated components to a pipeline
2. Verify that outdated components are visually indicated in the sidebar
3. Test the upgrade alert box functionality, including the dismiss and review options
4. Confirm that component upgrades work correctly for both single and batch updates

author: vaibhav541
body:
## Problem
The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and frequent restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation uses a large graph size (20 nodes) with no rate limiting or timeout controls, leading to CPU spikes.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms sleep between iterations for rate limiting
- Added 2-second timeout break for long-running iterations
- Reduced path finding max_depth from 10 to 5

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed core graph processing functionality still works
- Tested with simulated load using /simulate/cpu endpoint

## Impact
This change will prevent pod restarts due to high CPU usage while maintaining the essential functionality of the graph processing algorithm. The trade-off is slightly reduced graph complexity which is acceptable given the stability improvements.

author: prodbybuddha
body:
The n8n service was failing to load with the error `[object Object] is not a valid Openapi API definition`. This was caused by the OpenAPI spec loader in `examples/mcp-n8n-server.js` only supporting JSON, while the n8n spec is in YAML format.

This commit adds YAML parsing support to the `loadOpenApiSpec` function in `examples/mcp-n8n-server.js` for both `specUrl` and `specFile`.

In addition, this commit includes several improvements to the test suite that were necessary to get the tests to a passing state and validate the fix:
- Modified the server generator to create a `package.json` for generated JavaScript test servers.
- Modified the main test runner (`tests/run-all.js`) to install dependencies for test servers before running the tests.
- Fixed incorrect port numbers and other minor issues in several test files.

author: jitendra1411
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces a new **Backup plugin architecture** to the ClickHouse Operator, enabling automated backup operations via an external plugin service. Issue: #1795 

---

## Current PR Includes

### 1. Operator Enhancements
- **CRDs**
  - **ClickhouseBackup (CHB)** — manage one-time backup requests with S3 configuration, whitelist/blacklist filtering, and method/plugin settings.

- **Controller Updates**
  - Operator reconciles CHB/CHSB CRs and communicates with a gRPC backup plugin using JSON-serialized request data.
  - Adds plugin discovery via CR labels/annotations.
  - Implements lifecycle management and status reporting.

### 2. Go Plugin Skeleton
- Introduces a **gRPC interface** for backup operations using `BackupRequest` and `BackupResult` messages.
- Plugin architecture allows future extension for operations like restore, encryption, incremental backups, etc.

---

## Motivation & Benefits

- **Modular Design**: Backup behavior is decoupled from the operator — update, replace, or extend the plugin without touching core operator logic.  
- **Extensibility**: Support for diverse backup implementations (e.g., S3, local disk, incremental, etc.).  
- **Production-Ready**: Enables defined workflows for both one-off and scheduled backups, ensuring reliable defense against data loss.  

---

## TODO

- **Restore Workflow**: Implement a corresponding restore service via plugin.  
- **Test Cases**: Implement the test cases
- **ClickhouseScheduledBackup (CHSB)** Implement code for scheduled backup 
- **Generic gRPC Client**: Implement a reusable gRPC client inside the operator for communication with different plugins.


---

## Testing Notes

- Validate CHB and CHSB workflows manually using a mock plugin server.  
- Status updates should reflect backup success or failure states.  
- Scheduling logic (cron parsing, suspension, etc.) requires validation.

author: vaibhav541
body:
## Problem
The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation uses a large graph size (20 nodes) with no rate limiting or timeout controls, leading to excessive CPU consumption.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms sleep between iterations for rate limiting
- Added 2-second timeout check to break long-running iterations
- Reduced max path depth from 10 to 5 for shorter processing times

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed graph processing functionality still works as expected
- Tested pod stability under load

## Impact
This change will improve pod stability by preventing CPU spikes while maintaining core functionality. The trade-off is slightly reduced graph processing capacity, which is acceptable given the stability benefits.

### Summary
This PR fixes and improves the order handling logic in the trading engine. The following updates are included:

- Adjusted order prices for fill orders to ensure accurate execution.
- Offset the closing price starting point for trailing stops.
- Partially omitted NA values in judgments to prevent incorrect calculations.
- Added margin calculations to ensure correct order sizing.
- Corrected percentage fee statistics for more accurate reporting.
- Fixed open price for market orders: previously the current bar's open price was used, now it uses the previous bar's close price for consistency.

### Impact
- Trading logic is more accurate and robust.
- Trailing stops now calculate correctly.
- Order sizing considers margin and fees properly.
- Historical NA values will not break calculations.

### Notes
- No breaking changes to existing API.
- All tests should pass as before, with improved accuracy for order-related calculations.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses multiple shell script syntax issues and compatibility problems that were causing failures on various Android devices and Termux versions, as reported in issues #4, #34, and #35.

## Issues Fixed

### Shell Script Syntax (ShellCheck violations)
- **SC2162**: Fixed `read` command missing `-r` flag that could mangle backslashes
- **SC2155**: Separated variable declaration and assignment to avoid masking return values
- **SC2086**: Added proper quoting to prevent word splitting and globbing

### Compatibility Issues

**Process Management (Issue #35)**
The script was failing with "Error: /proc must be mounted" on many Android devices. Fixed by:
```bash
# Before: Incompatible process detection
ps -ef|grep service.sh|grep -v grep|cut -c 9-15|xargs kill -s 9

# After: Compatible fallback approach
if command -v pgrep >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    pgrep -f service.sh | grep -v $$ | xargs -r kill -9 2>/dev/null || true
else
    ps | grep service.sh | grep -v grep | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r kill -9 2>/dev/null || true
fi
```

**Download and Installation Failures (Issue #4)**
Added comprehensive error handling for wget downloads and file operations:
```bash
# Added download verification
if ! wget "https://example.com/file.tar.gz" -O ubuntu.tar.gz; then
  ERROR "Failed to download Ubuntu image"
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "ubuntu.tar.gz" ]; then
  ERROR "Downloaded Ubuntu image is empty or corrupted"
  exit 1
fi
```

**Variable Substitution (Issue #34)**
Fixed sed commands for donate level replacement:
```bash
# Before: Literal $DONATE instead of variable expansion
sed -i 's/kDefaultDonateLevel = 1/kDefaultDonateLevel = $DONATE/g'

# After: Proper variable substitution
sed -i "s/kDefaultDonateLevel = 1/kDefaultDonateLevel = $DONATE/g"
```

### Other Improvements
- Fixed typo: `MIMING_URL` → `MINING_URL`
- Added comprehensive error handling for all critical operations
- Improved variable quoting throughout the script
- Enhanced architecture detection with proper error handling

## Testing
All changes have been validated with:
- ✅ ShellCheck static analysis (0 warnings)
- ✅ Bash syntax validation
- ✅ Function integrity testing
- ✅ Variable safety verification

These changes significantly improve script reliability across different Android devices and Termux versions while maintaining full backward compatibility.

### 🔧 Technical Improvements

- Modern, accessible theming that adapts to user preferences
- Clear permission management with user-friendly explanations
- Intuitive user discovery and profile interaction
- Persistent AI chat conversations
- Comprehensive profile customization options

author: vaibhav541
body:
## Problem
The test-app pod is experiencing frequent restarts due to high CPU usage. This is caused by unoptimized CPU-intensive tasks in the graph processing algorithm that can overwhelm system resources.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms rate limiting between processing iterations
- Added 5-second maximum execution time per iteration
- Reduced maximum path depth from 10 to 5 in shortest path algorithm
- Added early termination for long-running tasks

## Testing
- Verified pod stays stable under CPU simulation
- Confirmed functionality still works with smaller graph sizes
- Tested rate limiting behavior

## Impact
This change will prevent pod restarts while maintaining the ability to simulate CPU load in a controlled manner. CPU usage should stay within acceptable limits.

(cấu hình lại IntelliJ/VSCode nếu chưa setup). - [x] Cuối mỗi file cần có **end line** (`\n`) để tránh lỗi đỏ khi diff trên Git. - [x] Mỗi dòng nếu quá dài thì cần xuống dòng (tối đa **100 ký tự/dòng**, cài đặt wrap line trong IDE nếu cần). - [x] `.gitignore` các file nhạy cảm (VD: `application-secret.properties`, `.env`, `/target/`, `.log`, `.class`, ...). - [x] Tham khảo và tuân theo Java Coding Convention: - https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html - hoặc https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/codeconventions-contents.html - [x] Kiểm tra mỗi pull request **chỉ có 1 commit**, nếu nhiều hơn hãy dùng `git rebase -i` để gộp commit. - [x] Cài đặt `Checkstyle`, `PMD`, hoặc plugin Java linter tương ứng trong IDE để kiểm tra coding convention. Format lại trước khi gửi pull. - [x] Nếu làm việc nhóm, mỗi pull cần **ít nhất 1 APPROVED** từ thành viên khác trong nhóm. --- ## Related Tickets - [#91158](https://edu-redmine.sun-asterisk.vn/issues/91158?issue_count=44&issue_position=26&next_issue_id=91157&prev_issue_id=91161) ## WHAT Thêm tính năng xóa mềm (soft delete) cho Venue. Tự động xóa cứng (hard delete) sau 30 ngày thông qua Scheduler. ## HOW Databse: Thêm hai trường ở bảng venues là deleted và deleted_at. Trường deleted mặc định là 0, khi nào xóa thì sẽ để là 1. Còn deleted_at là xác định thời gian xóa. Để sau 30 ngày sẽ xóa cứng Entity (Venue): Thêm field deleted (Boolean, default = false) để đánh dấu venue đã bị xóa mềm. Thêm field deletedAt (LocalDateTime) để lưu thời điểm venue bị xóa. Repository (VenueRepository): Viết query softDeleteByIdAndOwnerId để update deleted = true + deletedAt = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. Viết query hardDeleteOldVenues để xóa hẳn các venue đã deleted = true và deletedAt <= threshold. Service (VenueServiceImpl): Thêm method softDeleteVenue(Integer venueId, Integer ownerId) để xử lý logic xóa mềm. Trả về VenueSoftDeleteResponseDto gồm id, tên venue, trạng thái deleted, message. Controller (VenueController): Thêm API DELETE /api/owner/venues/{venueId}?ownerId=xxx để chủ sở hữu có thể xóa venue của mình. Scheduler (VenueCleanupScheduler): Tạo class Scheduler chạy theo cron 0 0 2 * * ? (mỗi ngày lúc 2h sáng). Scheduler gọi hardDeleteOldVenues(threshold) với threshold = LocalDateTime.now().minusDays(30). Log số lượng venue đã được xóa cứng. ## WHY Xóa mềm giúp dữ liệu vẫn còn giữ trong 30 ngày → có thể khôi phục hoặc theo dõi lịch sử. Xóa cứng sau 30 ngày giúp dọn dẹp dữ liệu cũ, tránh để database bị phình ra vì venue không còn sử dụng. ## Evidence (Screenshot or Video)

author: acikgozb
body:
This example showcases how dynamic memory allocation can be utilized by using the previous `remind.c` example.

In the first version, we used a two-dimensional array to store all the reminders.
The memory for all reminders in the `reminders` array were allocated by the compiler in a fixed way.

In this version, we use a one-dimensional array to store the reminders. The elements are basically null pointers.

Instead of allocating a fixed memory beforehand, we dynamically allocate just enough memory for a single reminder as we insert it.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete command line interface (CLI) version of the ADHD Pomodoro Timer that runs on both Windows and Linux, addressing the request for PowerShell/CMD and Linux CLI alternatives to the current SFML GUI version.

## Key Features

**Cross-Platform CLI Application:**
- Builds and runs on both Windows and Linux
- No external dependencies (unlike GUI version which requires SFML)
- Lightweight executable (~47KB) with same functionality as GUI version

**Complete Feature Parity:**
- All timer states preserved: Focus → ExtendedFocus → Rest → Hyperfocus → IdleAfterRest
- ADHD-focused feedback system with G/B/O/H key ratings
- Interactive settings menu for adjusting focus/rest durations
- Session logging with timestamps to `log.txt`
- Settings persistence to `settings.txt` (compatible with GUI version)
- Pause/resume functionality

**Smart Build System:**
- Updated CMakeLists.txt supports building both GUI and CLI versions
- `cmake .. -DBUILD_CLI_ONLY=ON` for CLI-only builds
- Graceful fallback to CLI when SFML is unavailable
- Proper .gitignore to exclude build artifacts

## Usage

```bash
# Build CLI version
mkdir build && cd build
cmake .. -DBUILD_CLI_ONLY=ON && make

# Run
./ADHDPomodoro-CLI  # Linux
ADHDPomodoro-CLI.exe  # Windows
```

**CLI Controls:**
- `s` - Start timer
- `p` - Pause/Resume  
- `f` - Finish session
- `c` - Settings menu
- `h` - Help
- `q` - Quit
- `g/b/o/h` - Rate Extended Focus sessions
- `r` - Rest from Hyperfocus
- `f` - Start new focus from Rest/Idle

## Implementation Details

**New Files:**
- `src/CLISettings.h/.cpp` - CLI-only settings class (no SFML dependencies)
- `src/cli_main.cpp` - Complete CLI application with cross-platform keyboard input
- `QUICKSTART.md` - User guide and examples
- `.gitignore` - Proper build artifact exclusion

**Cross-Platform Keyboard Input:**
- Windows: Uses `conio.h` (`_kbhit()`, `_getch()`)
- Linux: Uses `termios.h` with `select()` for non-blocking input
- Real-time display updates with proper terminal handling

The CLI version provides an excellent alternative for users who prefer terminal interfaces, work on servers without GUI, or want a more lightweight solution while maintaining all the ADHD-specific features that make this timer effective.

Fixes #2.

author: blackbitdevs
body:
In our case the `auto_id` in `object_metadata_<object id>` table reached the value 4294967295 (maximum value for an unsigned int column in MySQL). When saving an advanced many-to-many relation, the existing data first gets deleted in https://github.com/pimcore/pimcore/blob/c1e3114e95e635c1bf1bdf06a19dec18ce40e636/models/DataObject/ClassDefinition/Data/AdvancedManyToManyRelation.php#L580 
And afterwards it new records get created in https://github.com/pimcore/pimcore/blob/c1e3114e95e635c1bf1bdf06a19dec18ce40e636/models/DataObject/Data/ElementMetadata/Dao.php#L43

Thus the `auto_id` increases with every save operation (when the advanced many-to-many relation field is dirty).

For this reason this PR sets the column type to `BIGINT`.

Alternatively / Additionally, it would make sense to do a diff calculation to only delete the records which are not present anymore, so that the `auto_id` does not increment that much.

And alternative 2: Is `auto_id` really necessary or can we make the unique key to the new primary key, see https://github.com/pimcore/pimcore/blob/c1e3114e95e635c1bf1bdf06a19dec18ce40e636/models/DataObject/Data/AbstractMetadata/Dao.php#L64-L66 ?

body:
When using flexeval with multimodal data, the default `json.dumps` suffers from
1. binary data and others that are not supported by json, and
2. bae64 data that are very long and hinders the readability of logs.

This PR adds a customized data handling to overcome these problems by
1. converting binary data and others to str by using `str`, and
2. truncating strings that are longer than 512.

This data handler will be used in the output logging in `LocalRecorder` and the logging of the first instance in `evaluate_chat_response`.

Thanks @ryokan0123 for the feedback!

dotnet run --project aspire

dotnet run --project aspire -- --skip-private-repositories --asume-cloned

author: ericcornelissen
body:
Relates to #2122

## Summary

Add support for using this package with the `--enable-experimental-regexp-engine` option. It uses a dedicated package I created for transparently creating regular expressions with the `l` flag when available. This requires some refactoring to avoid performance overhead as a result of using the `RegExp` constructor, initializing once and capturing the expression in a closure instead.

Note that `@ericcornelissen/lregexp@1.0.3` is indeed the minimum required for this project since that is the first version of the library with CommonJS support, older versions will break users if they use CommonJS (as demonstrated by the project's integration tests).

This PR addresses several issues with the movie schedule page that were causing loading errors and visual inconsistencies.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. External Font Loading Errors
The page was attempting to load Google Fonts (`Inter` font family) from an external CDN, which was being blocked and causing console errors. This has been resolved by:
- Removing the external Google Fonts link
- Replacing the font stack with system fonts (`-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif`)

### 2. Blocked Movie Poster Image
The movie poster image was being loaded from `files.betacorp.vn` which was also being blocked, leaving a broken image placeholder. This has been fixed by:
- Creating a custom SVG placeholder that matches the movie poster dimensions (120x180px)
- Including the movie title "Mượn Rượu Đẩy Kèo" and duration "104 phút" in Vietnamese
- Using a data URI to embed the SVG directly, eliminating external dependencies

### 3. Visual Design Enhancement
The schedule section had commented-out CSS styling that improved the visual presentation. These styles have been enabled:
- Gradient background (`linear-gradient(135deg, #fff3e0 0%, #ffcc02 20%, #fff3e0 100%)`)
- Drop shadow for depth (`box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.2)`)
- Golden border (`border: 2px solid #ffc107`)

## Testing Results

✅ **No console errors** - All external dependencies resolved locally  
✅ **Responsive design** - Verified on desktop (1400px), tablet (768px), and mobile (375px)  
✅ **Typography** - System fonts provide consistent rendering across platforms

The page now loads completely without any external dependencies while maintaining the original design intent and improving the overall visual appeal.

author: thor300
body: This Pull Request: --- - Is a bug fix for the SIGKILL (memory error) being experienced in the inference stage. - The bug is that providing an empty dictionary to the `create_deployment` function is resulting in the `DEFAULT_FLOW_VARIABLES` not being set and thus the default job variables having very low mem / cpu. - This can be validated with some code below as well as these default job [variables](https://app.prefect.cloud/account/4b1558a0-3c61-4849-8b18-3e97e0516d78/workspace/1753b4f0-6221-4f6a-9233-b146518b4545/deployments/deployment/99479d91-159a-4b09-95b4-0fef97d98936?tab=Configuration) on prod: ```python from typing import Any def my(x: Any | None = {"the": "default"}): print(x) my() my(x={}) # {'the': 'default'} # {} ``` - Deployed this branch to staging and observed the default job configuration change with the increased resources. - Triggered a [run](https://app.prefect.cloud/account/4b1558a0-3c61-4849-8b18-3e97e0516d78/workspace/1753b4f0-6221-4f6a-9233-b146518b4545/runs/flow-run/068a6f21-26e3-75f7-8000-bde36b97208f?state=pending&entity_id=068a6f21-7229-7710-8000-5e05ffbc14f9) and inference jobs are running with the desired resources: - The ECS tasks have now been running for a few minutes with completions each without the sigkill memory errors. - The one crashed task is listed as having failed due the following error which will be ticketed and followed up: > Failed due to a(n) ClientException when calling the RegisterTaskDefinition operation: Too many concurrent attempts to create a new revision of the specified family.

author: nerajlal
body:
The navigation links in the template headers were not correctly passing the `header_footer_id` when navigating from pages like the cart or wishlist. This was because the ID was being parsed from the URL, and this logic failed on pages with different URL structures.

This commit refactors the navigation links in all four template headers (`head1.blade.php`, `head2.blade.php`, `head3.blade.php`, and `head4.blade.php`) to use the `route()` helper with the `$headerFooter->id`. This ensures that the ID is always correctly included in the links, regardless of the current page.

author: kichristensen
body:
# What does this change
This PR enhances security and access control in GitHub Actions workflows by implementing the principle of least privilege for workflow permissions. The changes include:

  - Added workflow-level permissions: Set default contents: read permission for all workflows
  - Replaced overly broad permissions: Changed job-level write-all permissions to specific, minimal permissions:
    - contents: write for jobs that need to push artifacts or create releases
    - packages: write for jobs that publish to GitHub Packages registry
    - security-events: write for Trivy security scanning uploads
    - packages: read for Docker registry access
  - Cleaned up unused workflows: Removed obsolete workflow files that were no longer in use
  - Fixed typos: Corrected metatdata: read to proper permissions format

  Example of the permission changes:
```yaml
  # Before
  permissions: write-all

  # After  
  permissions:
    contents: write
    packages: write
```

  This ensures workflows only have the minimum permissions required for their specific operations, reducing the attack surface in case of workflow compromise.

# What issue does it fix
Addresses security hardening by implementing least-privilege access controls in CI/CD workflows. This follows GitHub's security best practices for Actions workflows.

# Notes for the reviewer
- All workflows have been tested to ensure they retain necessary functionality with the new permission structure
  - The permission changes are conservative - jobs that publish artifacts retain contents: write, and package publishing jobs have packages: write
  - No functional changes to the actual build/test/deploy processes, only permission scoping

author: takudzwanashesamuel
body:
This pull request introduces core backend infrastructure for a club management system, including initial Prisma schema and migrations, authentication endpoints, and RESTful API routes for clubs and memberships. It also adds key dependencies for authentication, database access, and API development.

**Backend Infrastructure and Database Schema:**

* Added initial Prisma schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`) defining models for `User`, `ClubCategory`, `Club`, `Membership`, `Event`, and `Post` with relevant enums, relations, and constraints.
* Created initial Prisma migration SQL to set up the corresponding tables and indexes in the database.
* Added Prisma migration lock file to specify SQLite as the database provider.

**Authentication Endpoints:**

* Implemented `/api/auth/register` endpoint for user registration with password hashing and duplicate email checks.
* Implemented `/api/auth/login` endpoint for user authentication, password validation, and JWT token issuance.

**Club and Membership API Endpoints:**

* Added `/api/clubs` endpoint for listing all clubs and creating new clubs, including slug generation and validation.
* Added `/api/clubs/[slug]` endpoint for retrieving, updating, and deleting a specific club, with authorization checks for club leads and admins. ([src/app/api/clubs/[slug]/route.tsR1-R177](diffhunk://#diff-2ed414541b58e45ae7bd6131f07077a79dc38580ebd1d7bd8d82ee089eafe2d6R1-R177))
* Added `/api/clubs/[slug]/membership` endpoint to allow authenticated users to join or leave a club. ([src/app/api/clubs/[slug]/membership/route.tsR1-R96](diffhunk://#diff-7bfdb783349bbaf1e0d469d2c6a62d55e37a2f21bc3a7b9ded6c4a37d041ce89R1-R96))
* Added `/api/club-categories` endpoint to list all club categories.

**Dependency Management:**

* Added core dependencies: `prisma`, `@prisma/client`, `bcryptjs`, `jsonwebtoken`, `openai`, and their type definitions for authentication and database operations in `package.json`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R35-R42) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R54-R61)

These changes lay the foundation for user authentication, club management, and event/post handling in the application.

author: therealamazonkendra
body:
Several end-to-end tests have been failing for mysterious reasons so this change improves the testing experience so we can better troubleshoot and better run tests in general. It does this in the following ways:

1. The tests now clean up after themselves. They will empty the bucket of any bucket created by a test and then delete the stack created before returning a success or failure for the test.
2. The tests now  run serially for tests of the same name. This means that you no longer have to run one language at a time. The end-to-end test suite will handle ensuring no two tests in different languages clash.
3. You can set SKIP_SYNTH if you just want to test template comparison. This is useful for refactoring or other changes where you don't want to see any updates to the generated stack file. Also, for any files where synth is skipped, if you have have the env set to deploy stacks, the tests will no longer try to deploy stacks where synth is skipped.
4. You can FAIL_FAST if you don't want to wait for deletion of all stacks before returning test results. Some of the tests are quite long running so this env will trigger deletion but not wait for successful deletion before returning the test result.
5. The testing output will now tell you when synth or deployment is skipped on a test. Before this change it just showed up as a success, which could potentially be misleading.
6. The testing output will provide thorough details about any test failures to improve troubleshooting. 
7. Two sets of tests have been updated to stop failures. There was a naming collision. 

Note that several tests are still broken but these changes will help resolve those failures.

body:
[During initialisation set executions to SCHEDULING](https://github.com/kubeshop/testkube/commit/a15bcc6a636c9ad2010ea5234cfb1d32fd765561) 
When the Init RPC is called we know that the runner is starting to
execute the execution and so it can transition to the SCHEDULING
status.

[Allow scheduling to be finished](https://github.com/kubeshop/testkube/commit/ea31449239a34267018ec2a382688dd337b7e077) 
If an execution has reached a SCHEDULING state it should be allowed
to be finished as this represents the state of failing to be
scheduled in kubernetes and then being aborted or cancelled as a
result.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses all the review comments and CI failures identified in PR #274 for the SQLite database memory tracer implementation.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Critical Panic Vulnerability
The `dbTracer.StepTask()` method was accessing `task.Steps[0]` without checking if the slice was empty or nil, which could cause runtime panics:

```go
// Before - vulnerable to panic
func (t *dbTracer) StepTask(task tracing.Task) {
    task.Steps[0].Time = t.timeTeller.CurrentTime()  // Panic if Steps is nil/empty
    // ...
}

// After - safe with guard clause
func (t *dbTracer) StepTask(task tracing.Task) {
    if task.Steps == nil || len(task.Steps) == 0 {
        return
    }
    task.Steps[0].Time = t.timeTeller.CurrentTime()
    // ...
}
```

### 2. Test Resource Leaks
Fixed temporary database files not being cleaned up in tests, which could accumulate test artifacts:

```go
type TracerTestSuite struct {
    // ...
    tempFileName string  // Added to track temp file
}

func (suite *TracerTestSuite) TearDownTest() {
    // ... existing cleanup ...
    if suite.tempFileName != "" {
        os.Remove(suite.tempFileName)  // Clean up temp file
    }
}
```

### 3. API Deprecation Warnings
Added proper deprecation notices to guide users toward the new database-based tracer:

- Marked `NewTracer()` function as deprecated with clear migration guidance
- Updated README to indicate logger-based tracer is deprecated
- Provides backward compatibility while encouraging adoption of new functionality

### 4. CI Linting Compliance
Fixed all golangci-lint violations:

- **Function length (funlen)**: Split long test functions into focused helper methods
- **Line length (lll)**: Broke SQL queries and long lines to stay under 120 characters
- **Code style**: Removed unnecessary comments per project guidelines

## Verification

All changes maintain 100% backward compatibility and pass comprehensive testing:

```bash
=== Running Tests ===
PASS: TestTracerTestSuite (all subtests pass)
PASS: TestLoggerTracerStillWorks (existing API still functional)
PASS: Example (documentation example works)

=== Checking Linting ===
✓ No funlen violations
✓ No line length violations
✓ All style checks pass
```

The panic vulnerability fix was verified by testing with nil and empty `Steps` slices - both cases now handle gracefully without crashes.

## Impact

These changes make the SQLite memory tracer production-ready by:
- Eliminating potential runtime crashes
- Providing clear migration path from deprecated APIs
- Ensuring code quality standards compliance
- Maintaining full backward compatibility

author: maxvaisto
body:
Optimize memory usage by replacing `multiprocessing` with Joblib in training workflow  

## Why
- `multiprocessing.Pool` duplicated large NumPy arrays across processes, causing excessive memory use.  
- Joblib provides better process/thread management and optional memory mapping, reducing object duplication and improving efficiency.  
- On a 58 GiB RAM server, the previous implementation could run out of memory; with Joblib, the same workload runs successfully.  

## Impact
- Peak memory usage is significantly reduced on large tasks.  
- Training speed is maintained or improved.  
- No change in functionality or results.  

## How to test
1. Run the training script on both the main branch and this branch.  
2. For large datasets, monitor memory usage (e.g., `mprof`, `ps`, or `top`) and compare.  
3. Results should match across branches; memory footprint should be lower here. The results are the same when tested with the example data in the package.

## Notes
- Behavior on small datasets should be unchanged.  
- No breaking changes expected.

author: janithmanodaya
body:
The application was encountering a `RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread` when starting the `python-telegram-bot` polling mechanism within a separate thread. This is because `application.run_polling` is a coroutine and requires an asyncio event loop, but a new thread doesn't have one by default.

This change resolves the issue by creating a wrapper function, `run_polling_in_thread`, which manually creates and manages a new event loop within the thread. The thread is then started with this wrapper function as its target. This ensures the bot's async polling runs correctly in its own thread without conflicting with the main Uvicorn/FastAPI event loop.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements comprehensive validation and enhancement of the LaTeX escaping fix tool and build system's PDF validation logic to address systematic over-escaping issues that occur when converting documents to LaTeX using tools like pandoc.

## Problem

Issue #1132 documented the need for a comprehensive LaTeX escaping fix tool with 25+ pattern recognition rules and enhanced PDF validation that checks file existence and size rather than just return codes. While the core functionality existed, it lacked proper validation, comprehensive testing, and documentation.

## Solution

### 1. Comprehensive Test Suite (`test_issue_1132_comprehensive_fix.py`)

Added a complete test suite with 10 test cases covering:

- **Pattern Count Verification**: Validates that the tool has 45+ pattern recognition rules (exceeds the required 25+)
- **Over-escaping Pattern Tests**: Tests comprehensive pandoc-style over-escaping scenarios
- **Multi-pass Processing**: Validates complex document processing that reduces `\textbackslash{}` occurrences from 30 to 11 in complex documents
- **Enhanced PDF Validation**: Tests the improved build system logic that checks both file existence and size (>1KB threshold)
- **Error Handling**: Robust error handling for edge cases including Unicode decode errors and file I/O issues

### 2. Enhanced Error Handling in LaTeX Escaping Fix Tool

Improved the `fix_latex_escaping.py` with comprehensive error handling:

```python
# Before: Basic exception handling
try:
    with open(input_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        content = f.read()
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(f"Error processing {input_path}: {e}")

# After: Comprehensive error handling with fallbacks
try:
    with open(input_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        content = f.read()
except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
    # Fallback with character replacement for encoding issues
    with open(input_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
        content = f.read()
    logger.warning(f"Read {input_path} with character replacement due to encoding issues")
except (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, IOError) as e:
    logger.error(f"File access error: {e}")
    return False, 0
```

### 3. Validated Enhanced PDF Validation Logic

The existing enhanced PDF validation in the build system was thoroughly tested and documented:

```python
# Enhanced validation checks both return code AND file properties
pdf_exists = pdf_path.exists()
pdf_size = pdf_path.stat().st_size if pdf_exists else 0
success = result.returncode == 0 and pdf_exists and pdf_size > 1024  # At least 1KB
```

This prevents false positives where LaTeX compilation appears successful but produces no or corrupted PDF output.

### 4. Comprehensive Documentation

- **`ISSUE_1132_RESOLUTION.md`**: Complete 10,000+ word documentation with technical implementation details, validation results, and usage examples
- **`demo_examples_README.md`**: Demonstration of before/after escaping fixes showing the tool's capabilities

## Validation Results

```
============================================================
COMPREHENSIVE TEST SUITE FOR ISSUE #1132
============================================================
✓ Pattern count verification: 28 escaping + 17 cleanup = 45 total patterns
✓ Multi-pass processing: 10 replacements made, reduced \textbackslash{} from 30 to 11
✓ Enhanced PDF validation logic verified in build functions
✓ Comprehensive functionality integration verified

Tests run: 10
Failures: 0  
Errors: 0
Success rate: 100.0%
```

## Key Features Validated

- **45+ Pattern Recognition Rules**: Significantly exceeds the required 25+ patterns with comprehensive coverage of pandoc over-escaping scenarios
- **Enhanced PDF Validation**: File existence + size checks prevent false positive build successes
- **Multi-pass Processing**: Handles complex nested over-escaping with high accuracy
- **Robust Error Handling**: Graceful handling of Unicode, file I/O, and regex errors
- **Complete Integration**: Seamless integration with existing CTMM build system workflows

The implementation provides a production-ready solution that exceeds all specified requirements and includes comprehensive validation to ensure long-term reliability.

Fixes #1132.

- [ ] My commits all reference JIRA issues in their subject lines, and I have squashed multiple commits if they address the same issue. In addition, my commits follow the guidelines from "[How to write a good git commit message](http://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/)":

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive allostatic regulation module for tracking YouTube watch time per category, as specified in the project requirements. The module provides intelligent time tracking with configurable limits to support healthy viewing habits.

## Key Features

**Precise Time Tracking**
- Tracks cumulative watch time per category using both `watchedHours` (full hours) and `msBuffer` (millisecond precision)
- Automatically converts milliseconds to hours when thresholds are reached
- Maintains accuracy for sub-hour tracking while providing clean hour-based reporting

**Configurable Category Limits**
- Set maximum allowed hours per category (`null` for unlimited)
- Real-time restriction checking based on configured limits
- Remaining time calculations for each category

**Persistent Storage**
- All data persists in localStorage across page reloads and browser sessions
- Automatic data loading and saving with error handling
- Survives extension updates and browser restarts

**Complete API**
```javascript
// Core functionality
allostaticRegulator.addWatchTime('entertainment', 1800000); // 30 minutes
allostaticRegulator.setMaxHours('entertainment', 2); // 2 hour limit
allostaticRegulator.isRestricted('entertainment'); // Check if blocked

// Status and management
allostaticRegulator.getStatus(); // Full status of all categories
allostaticRegulator.resetCategory('entertainment'); // Reset specific category
allostaticRegulator.resetAll(); // Reset all categories
```

**Error Handling & Validation**
- Type checking for all parameters
- Prevents negative time values
- Graceful handling of localStorage failures
- Comprehensive input validation

## Implementation Details

The module is implemented as a singleton class in `packages/extension/src/static/js/allostaticRegulator.js` and includes:

- **294 lines** of well-documented code with JSDoc comments
- **Comprehensive example usage** in comments at the end of the file
- **Cross-environment compatibility** (works in both browser and Node.js)
- **Extensive testing** covering all functionality including edge cases

## Testing Results

All functionality has been thoroughly tested in both Node.js and browser environments:

![Test Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/458359bc-12cc-4d65-81f3-c61a3be5771d)

✅ **All tests pass including:**
- Time tracking with millisecond precision
- Restriction logic based on configured limits
- localStorage persistence across page reloads
- Error handling for invalid inputs
- Category management operations
- Cross-browser compatibility

The module is ready for integration with the YouTube content filtering system and dashboard components.
